topics.label: Introduction and learning objectives
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic frames the lecture within the cancer course and sets out its learning objectives.

topics.label: Cancer evolution and the origins of cancer-causing mutations
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics establish how mutations arising in susceptible cells can support clonal evolution within a permissive microenvironment.

topics.label: Environmental cancer risks and evidence for their contribution
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how environmental exposures contribute to cancer risk rather than attributing cancer solely to chance or inherited susceptibility.

topics.label: Infectious causes of cancer
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how infections can drive carcinogenesis, using Burkitt lymphoma as a detailed example of interacting infectious causes.

topics.label: Environmental carcinogens and mechanisms of DNA damage
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how environmental carcinogens produce DNA damage through processes whose effects depend on metabolism and tissue context.

topics.label: Tumour initiation and promotion
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics distinguish mutational initiation from the promotion of tumour growth and explain why a permissive environment matters.

topics.label: Tissue and developmental susceptibility, with a recap of carcinogenic mechanisms
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics complete the account of carcinogenesis by establishing the importance of target-cell susceptibility before consolidating the mechanisms discussed.

topics.label: Methods for investigating carcinogenicity
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how evidence of carcinogenicity can be obtained and why the available investigative methods have limitations.

topics.label: Closing summary and cancer risk–benefit decisions
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic closes the lecture by summarising its conclusions and placing cancer risks within everyday risk–benefit decisions.
